summary: EDGE invests in Australia-based quantum technology firm Q-CTRL TradeArabia
detail: EDGE, a UAE-based advanced technology group, has made a strategic investment in Q-CTRL, an Australian firm specializing in quantum technology. This move highlights the increasing global interest and capital flow into the nascent but potentially transformative field of quantum computing. Q-CTRL is recognized for developing quantum control infrastructure software, which is crucial for stabilizing and improving the performance of quantum computers, addressing one of the core challenges in the technology's development. The investment by EDGE suggests a strategic intent to secure a position in this cutting-edge sector, potentially leveraging quantum advancements for defense, aerospace, or other high-tech applications. Quantum computing, which harnesses quantum-mechanical phenomena like superposition and entanglement, promises to solve problems currently intractable for classical computers, with implications for drug discovery, materials science, cryptography, and complex optimization. Such investments are vital for funding the extensive research, development, and eventual commercialization required to bring quantum technologies to fruition.

title: Show HN: Isometric SF – A pixel-art map of the SF Bay Area
summary: Technical Write-up: https://www.justinchavez.com/blog/isometric-sf-how/ Hi HN! Showcasing this fun project. I took 1300 square miles of the SF Bay Area from Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles and transformed them into a cohesive pixel map. It's really fun to explore and stumble upon various famous landmarks like Apple …
detail: Developer Justin Chavez showcased 'Isometric SF,' a pixel-art map of the San Francisco Bay Area, created by transforming Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles into a stylized 2D representation. The project notably employed fine-tuned open-source AI models, specifically Qwen-Image-Edit 2511 LoRA and Klein 4B LoRA, to achieve the consistent pixel-art style. This approach significantly reduced the computational cost compared to using larger, more resource-intensive models, demonstrating the increasing accessibility and efficiency of AI tools for individual creators. The project highlights a creative application of AI for artistic data transformation, showcasing how machine learning can augment human creativity and make complex stylistic rendering more affordable. The ability to convert detailed 3D geographical data into a cohesive, stylized 2D format opens new avenues for digital art, interactive mapping, and game development, underscoring the practical utility of advanced AI techniques like Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for efficient model fine-tuning.

Following this acquisition, Deloitte launched a new dedicated company named Edisyl. This strategic move underscores Deloitte's commitment to expanding its capabilities in advanced AI, particularly within the rapidly evolving digital asset and blockchain ecosystem. By integrating Flipside's specialized AI expertise, Deloitte aims to enhance its offerings in data analytics, risk management, and strategic consulting for clients navigating the complexities of decentralized finance (DeFi) and other crypto-related ventures. The establishment of Edisyl signifies a focused effort to consolidate and further develop these AI-driven services, positioning Deloitte as a key provider of sophisticated solutions for emerging technologies. This acquisition reflects a broader trend among major consulting firms to acquire specialized tech capabilities to meet the growing demand from corporate and institutional clients for expertise in cutting-edge fields.
